text:
Whether Monzo’s paid plans are worth it depends on whether you will actively use the lifestyle perks or insurance bundled with them. For many people, **Monzo’s free tier is already one of the best current accounts in the UK**, meaning you should only pay if the perks clearly offset the subscription fee.

Monzo offers three paid tiers: **Extra**, **Perks**, and **Max**. 

---

### 1. Monzo Extra (£3/month / £36/year)
*Target: Power budgeters and spreadsheet users.*

* **What you get:** Unlimited connected external bank accounts and credit cards, virtual cards linked directly to Pots, advanced auto-roundups, custom spending categories, live auto-export to Google Sheets, and enhanced credit insights (TransUnion & Equifax).
* **Is it worth it?**
  * **Yes, if:** You want Monzo to act as your complete financial dashboard, love granular budgeting, or use virtual cards for subscriptions and online shopping safety.
  * **No, if:** You only do standard day-to-day spending. You can also get open-banking account aggregation for free via third-party apps like Snoop, and basic budgeting is already free on Monzo.

---

### 2. Monzo Perks (£9/month / £108/year)
*Target: Everyday spenders who can take advantage of lifestyle vouchers.*

* **What you get:** Everything in Extra, plus:
  * A free weekly Greggs treat (hot drink, sausage roll, or sweet treat).
  * An annual National Railcard (or similar partner perk).
  * Boosted interest rates on Monzo savings pots.
  * Higher fee-free cash withdrawals abroad and 3 fee-free cash deposits per month via PayPoint.
* **Is it worth it?**
  * **Yes, if:** You do the maths on the perks. A weekly Greggs item is worth ~£2–£2.50 per week (~£100+/year), and an annual Railcard saves £35/year. If you use both regularly, the plan pays for itself before factoring in the £3/month Extra tools.
  * **No, if:** You don’t regularly walk past a Greggs or travel by train. Don’t buy Perks purely for the boosted savings rate; you can almost always find comparable or higher easy-access savings rates elsewhere on the open market without paying a monthly fee.

---
